# Field { #clerq.Field }

```python
Field(
    label='',
    index=0,
    coupled_levels=None,
    factors=None,
    detuning=0.0,
    detuning_positive=True,
    counter_propagating=False,
    factor_doppler_shift=None,
    rabi_freq=1.0,
    rabi_freq_t_func=None,
    rabi_freq_t_args=None,
)
```

Field object to address the System object, describing the atomic levels
coupled, detuning and Rabi frequency function.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name                 | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|----------------------|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| label                | string | a name for the field e.g. "probe".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| index                | int    | index of the field, to reference within a System.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| coupled_levels       | list   | pairs of levels coupled by the field. e.g. [[0,1], [0,2]]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| factors              | list   | List of strength factors for each pair in coupled levels. Each is the (signed) dipole matrix element of the pair relative to the reference transition, e.g. a Clebsch-Gordan coefficient, so the squares sum to the line strength. The same factor scales the pair's coupling in the Hamiltonian and its coherence in the field's source term. |
| detuning             | float  | detuning of the fields from resonance with the coupled_levels transitions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| detuning_positive    | bool   | is the detuning positive?                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| counter_propagating  | bool   | if True, this field travels in the opposite direction to the forward-propagating solver direction. Sets factor_doppler_shift = -1.0. Orthogonal to detuning_positive.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| factor_doppler_shift | float  | multiplier applied to the thermal detuning Delta for each velocity class. Default 1.0 (co-propagating). Set to -1.0 for a counter-propagating field, or to an arbitrary float for schemes where wavelength differences matter (e.g. a three-photon ladder where k-vector magnitudes differ).                                                   |
| rabi_freq            | float  | Rabi frequency of the field on the transition.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| rabi_freq_t_func     | func   | Time-dependency of rabi_freq as function of time f(t, args)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| rabi_freq_t_args     | dict   | arguments to be passed to rabi_freq_t_func.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [get_json_dict](#clerq.Field.get_json_dict) | Return a dict representation of the Field object to be dumped to |
| [lower_levels](#clerq.Field.lower_levels) | Return the unique lower (ground) level indices coupled by this field. |
| [to_json_str](#clerq.Field.to_json_str) | Return a JSON string representation of the Field object. |
| [upper_levels](#clerq.Field.upper_levels) | Return the unique upper (excited) level indices coupled by this field. |

### get_json_dict { #clerq.Field.get_json_dict }

```python
Field.get_json_dict()
```

Return a dict representation of the Field object to be dumped to
JSON.

#### Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

For the rabi_freq_t_func attribute generated with
build_rabi_freq_t_func, a suffix for the index will have been
added. We remove that. e.g. e.g. ramp_onoff_0 -> ramp_onoff

### lower_levels { #clerq.Field.lower_levels }

```python
Field.lower_levels()
```

Return the unique lower (ground) level indices coupled by this field.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type        | Description                                                     |
|--------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | list\[int\] | Sorted list of unique indices ``c[0]`` from ``coupled_levels``. |
